week.worked: Monday night at Craven Cottage was the whole week. João Pedro and Rogers scored nineteen between them, and Calafiori added nine from a defender who has gone up in price since.
week.didnt: The expensive half did nothing. Haaland, B.Fernandes, Mbeumo and Shaw cost forty million pounds together and returned seven points between them. Kerkez played ninety minutes at Newcastle and got none of them.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Kerkez was taken off on 71 minutes at Anfield. Gvardiol costs a tenth of a million more and has kept his shirt through every shape Maresca has tried.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: Twenty points from a £4.0m defender, and Hull have now kept two clean sheets from two. Xabi's cheap slots are Diop and Hughes, who have two points between them.

big.call: Kerkez or Gvardiol, at about the same money
big.why: Kerkez was replaced on 71 minutes at home and has one point from two games. Gvardiol has started every week whatever shape City play, and City are at home to Coventry in GW3.

big.call: Three United men, and who wears the armband
big.why: B.Fernandes, Mbeumo and Shaw are £24.5m of one club, and Carrick answered the Hull defeat with "it's one game". GW4 is City at Old Trafford, so the armband is the cheaper half to settle.

week.worked: The cheap end carried him. Ajer at £4.5m and Schade at £6.0m are owned by nobody else in the room, and Szoboszlai, Calafiori and João Pedro did the rest. Nothing above £8.0m paid its way.
week.didnt: He captained a United midfielder and picked a United goalkeeper on the day United lost 2-0 at Hull. Two picks, one club, one bad afternoon, and Ballard blanked behind them.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: He carries two £4.0m Coventry defenders. Hull cost the same, have won both games and kept both clean sheets, and one of those wins was at Coventry.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He owns an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Nobody in the room has fixed that in three weeks of the brain saying so.

big.call: Two £4.0m Coventry defenders, with City away next
big.why: Coventry have no points and no goals, and GW3 is the Etihad. The two £4.0m Hull defenders have thirty-six points between them and won at Coventry on Saturday. Same price, opposite evidence.

big.call: Lammens, or the £5.0m keeper with two clean sheets
big.why: Same price. Lammens stands behind the defence that lost at Hull to two set plays. Trafford has kept two from two and faces Brentford at Elland Road, so the answer arrives before Friday.

week.worked: The best mid-price spine of the five. Ndiaye, Szoboszlai, Rogers, Calafiori and João Pedro all returned, most of his points came from players between £5.5m and £7.5m, and he spent no chip to get them.
week.didnt: Twelve points sat on his bench, nine of them Gvardiol, who started at left-back for City. It was the biggest bench score in the room, and it was bigger than the gap to the man leading it.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: He already owns Gvardiol, so he has watched this side up close. Cherki costs about what Rogers does and has twenty-two points to Rogers' eight.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: He owns the Everton midfielder. This is the same club bought from the other end, and Tarkowski has eighteen points and a late goal at Bournemouth.

big.call: Two Spurs goalkeepers, one bottom of the table
big.why: Kinsky starts and Dubravka sits behind him, so both of his goalkeeper slots are at one club. Spurs have spent £300m, lost at home to Newcastle and are bottom with no clean sheet.

big.call: Ndiaye, with the window shutting Tuesday
big.why: City are interested, Moyes says he is not encouraging a bid, and Forest have bid £40m for another Everton midfielder. The window shuts three days before the GW3 deadline.

week.worked: Arsenal paid him. Mosquera, Tzolis and Havertz each returned six from three picks costing under twenty million together, and João Pedro added eleven.
week.didnt: Two of his fifteen had no game to play in. Palestra and Aït-Nouri were not in their clubs' matchday squads, so they were slots rather than players, and the armband on Haaland came back with four points.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: He pays £8.5m for Semenyo on City's left. Cherki is a million cheaper, plays in the same team and has three times the points.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £6.0m and 3% owned, and he scored at Spurs. Newcastle have the kindest six-game run on the ticker and The Special One owns nobody there.

big.why: He is the only one who moved it to João Pedro. In GW3 Chelsea go to Arsenal, their hardest fixture in the next six, and City are at home to Coventry, one of the softest anybody has.

big.call: Aït-Nouri, a slot rather than a player
big.why: A £5.4m City defender with no points and 0.7% ownership, behind O'Reilly and Gvardiol in a back line Maresca rearranges every week. That is a bench place doing no work at all.

week.worked: Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, Calafiori and João Pedro all returned, and he leads the five without owning a single player the other four could not have bought.
week.didnt: Cash returned minus one, and Villa have been taken apart around him in the week since. Maguire managed one point, and the chip that put him top was spent on a bench worth six.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: His defence is Calafiori, Cash, Maguire, Konsa and Diop, and three of those clubs are being rebuilt in public. Gvardiol is the one City defender whose job has not moved.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: He owns Ndiaye already. Tarkowski is eighteen points at £6.0m from the same club, and Everton away has paid for two seasons now.

big.call: Konsa on the bench, Cash in the team
big.why: Two £4.5m defenders, and he has the Villa one starting. Arsenal are missing Saliba and Timber, Villa have sold Watkins, Konsa and Martinez, and Cash has minus one point.

big.call: Maguire, and a £5.0m that has returned one point
big.why: United lost at Hull to two headers with him in the middle of them, and GW4 is City at Old Trafford. The two £4.0m Hull defenders have thirty-six points between them at a lower price.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: Twenty-two points, the most of any midfielder in the game, and not one of the five owns him. The trigger was one start. He got it, scored twice, and ownership has climbed since.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still the miss of the season. Thirteen on the opening night, the penalties, and a Chelsea side being built around him. Ownership has risen for a fortnight while all five stood still.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: Twenty points from the cheapest defender price in the game, and Hull have won both games without conceding. The brain declined this pick after one haul. Two weeks on that looks like the wrong call.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: Eighteen points at £6.0m and the late equaliser at Bournemouth. Nobody in the five owns him and Everton have a soft run once the Arsenal week is gone.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £6.0m and 3% owned. He scored at Spurs and Newcastle have the kindest six-game run on the ticker. Nobody in the room owns a Newcastle player.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: All five own an Arsenal defender. None owns the Arsenal player who has outscored them, at £6.6m, and Arsenal host Chelsea in GW3.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Thirteen points and the penalties on the opening night, then a start and the assist for the second in the cup, with his manager framing the whole side around him.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Eleven points, a rise to £7.6m and the number nine shirt — though Welbeck scoring on Thursday is the first evidence that the minutes are shared rather than owned.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box, and 67.6% ownership becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Tapped in on debut, got the full ninety, then started again in the cup and hit the bar — Chelsea keep picking him while Caicedo is out.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide or on the bench once Chelsea’s central midfield is whole again.

verdicts.name: Welbeck
verdicts.why: Headed the opener against Luton at 35 from a Gusto cross, his first since joining, and was singled out by his manager as the patient one who does what he does best.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. A £6.0m forward at 1% ownership who starts ahead of a 67%-owned one is a differential; one who comes on for him is not.

verdicts.name: Sánchez
verdicts.why: Alonso dropped him after the Fulham win, Chelsea signed Martinez for £7.5m, and he is reported unlikely to feature against Brighton and likely to be frozen out if he stays.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Nothing left to watch here.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Missed the cup tie too, so Chelsea have now played three competitive games with a makeshift pivot and Reece James in midfield.
verdicts.trigger: Ninety minutes against Brighton. Until then every Chelsea midfielder’s minutes are being set by an absence.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: Left out of the cup tie entirely with City expected to bid within 48 hours, and his manager’s answers did nothing to suggest he will play for Chelsea again.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Chelsea and starting in central midfield. Reported at £120m and possibly rising, that is not the way to bet.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: Six points at £6.0m from a back line that conceded twice, and Chelsea have just agreed £40m for another centre-back with the window four days from shutting.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against a Brighton side missing four forwards. If it does not come now, it is not coming.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: The move is done and the shirt looks done with it. Alonso ditched Sánchez after the Fulham win, and Chelsea have signed a 33-year-old World Cup winner on a two-year deal to start now.
verdicts.trigger: The player file moving him to Chelsea and a first clean sheet. Arsenal away in GW3 is not the fixture to price him on.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa have now sold Watkins, Konsa and Martinez and signed four players, and Arsenal come to Villa Park on Monday. A £4.5m defender in a back line being rebuilt in public.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or the window closing with the dressing room settled.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: Carrick called the criticism after Hull "lazy and easy" and defended his captain's leadership. That is a manager backing him, not a performance backing him.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Ipswich with the same shot profile, and £12.0m stops being a price and starts being a hole.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, and the Hull post-mortem points at shot quality rather than at the two set plays — the slower problem, not the quicker one.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking at home to Ipswich, which makes the GW4 sale automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Thirty-one, PFA Player of the Year in the same week his side lost at a promoted club, and still the position United are reported to want to reinforce before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: A left-back arriving before the deadline, or one week out of the side. Either ends a £4.5m pick whose entire case is that he never misses.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost at Hull to two headers, and there is a £5.0m goalkeeper with two clean sheets from two on the same shelf.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded — though with De Ligt out there is currently nobody to take the shirt.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United’s other centre-backs are fit.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, a rise to £5.6m, owned by four of the five and by 41.6% of the game — still the closest thing to a free lunch on the list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around, or the Champions League draw against Real Madrid producing genuine rotation.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.6m and a week later still nobody in the room owns him, which has stopped being an oversight and become a choice.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season’s injury record, or Arsenal’s returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal’s penalties at £9.5m, with barely 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation once Real Madrid appear on the calendar.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m and 7.3% ownership, in a forward line that has not settled around Gyökeres and whose club is still chasing another striker.
verdicts.trigger: Arsenal signing a forward before Tuesday, or two weeks as a substitute.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real and the seat is borrowed, and the £55m man behind him is now expected to play.
verdicts.trigger: Konsa starting at Villa Park. That is this pick ending, not threatening to.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: A £4.5m defender at 11% ownership expected to make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against the club he spent seven seasons at, in a defence missing both first-choice centre-backs.
verdicts.trigger: Named in the eleven and this is the cheapest starting defender at the champions. Left out again and the price is the only thing recommending him.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: Eleven points, the highest of any Arsenal defender, at £5.5m and 6.5% ownership — and the reason is the same injury list that put Mosquera in the side.
verdicts.trigger: Timber’s groin clearing, which returns him to a rotation option at a starter’s price.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six points and a debut that got noticed; 26% of the game is on him now and the price has not moved.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Back in central midfield against Forest and rated as the more alert Liverpool player defensively, on penalties at £7.0m, owned by three of the five.
verdicts.trigger: Mac Allister taking the pivot back after starting on Saturday, or a shift to right-back. Either halves the appeal.

verdicts.name: Gravenberch
verdicts.why: The trigger was a clean sheet against Forest or a week out of the pivot. He got neither the start nor the clean sheet — Mac Allister came back in and Liverpool conceded twice again.
verdicts.trigger: Settled by the team sheet. Revisit only if he starts twice in a row.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: A goal at Newcastle and the assist for Isak at Anfield, and City made formal contact on Saturday evening. Liverpool would rather sign another forward before letting him go.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday night passing with him still at Liverpool. Then seventeen points at £7.0m is the cheapest returning Liverpool attacker.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Poor at Anfield, sloppy on the ball and replaced by Tsimikas on 71 minutes. One point from two games, and Liverpool have conceded four.
verdicts.trigger: One start missed, and £5.5m for a full-back who does not attack is a sack.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two goals at Selhurst Park, the first a header from Semenyo's cross, and he has now scored in all six of his league games against Palace. Not one of the five had the armband on him.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through Cherki and Foden and past him.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back again and was inverted into midfield inside Maresca's 4-1-4-1. He is still the only City defender you can name in advance.
verdicts.trigger: O'Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back against his old club. That is one of the two games in the back line the trigger asked for.
verdicts.trigger: One more start in defence and £6.0m is a buy. Back into midfield and he is not a defender at all.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: The trigger was a start. He started at Palace and scored twice, the first after running through four defenders, and Maresca praised the pressing rather than the goals.
verdicts.trigger: Bouaddi settling into the midfield and Doku back on 5 September, and a manager famous for control deciding the free role costs too much off the ball.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Crossed for Haaland's opener and kept the wide role in a 4-1 win. First return of the season at £8.5m, and it was an assist rather than a shot.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks with Cherki and Foden taking the minutes, and £8.5m becomes a sack.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut and a rise to £5.6m, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate rather than the two assists, and Brentford have kept buying midfielders all window.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the threshold and he is the cheap midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Brentford have now signed a £40m left-back, their fifth arrival of the summer, on top of selling Pinnock and buying a centre-back. Eight points at £4.5m is real; the shirt is what is in doubt.
verdicts.trigger: One rotation, or Schuster starting a league game. A £4.5m centre-back at a club buying defenders holds his seat on loan.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what four of the five bought him for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds signing the £30m winger they are chasing and changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Trafford
verdicts.why: Two clean sheets from two opening games at £5.0m and 4.2% ownership, in the season’s cheapest goalkeeper bracket where everybody else is buying a floor.
verdicts.trigger: Brentford at Elland Road. A third clean sheet against a side that scored three at Spurs and this is the goalkeeper of the first quarter.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Moyes says he is not encouraging City's interest in a million years. Forest have now bid £40m for Armstrong instead, and Everton fans spent Saturday chanting about it.
verdicts.trigger: A bid accepted before Tuesday, which leaves two of the five holding a squad player at a bigger club.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Eleven points and the opener in a 2-0, then the pass for the first and the drive that made the second at Deepdale — Everton’s chances go through him at £6.5m and 4.5% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: A hat-trick and an assist in the cup after a header on the opening day, at £5.5m and 3% ownership, with his manager still saying publicly that the squad needs a forward.
verdicts.trigger: A league goal, or Everton signing the number nine Moyes keeps asking for. One of those makes him, one ends him.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: The trigger was a goal or a clean sheet at Bournemouth. He scored the late equaliser. Eighteen points at £6.0m from a defender nobody in the five owns.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a header or a clean sheet, and this goes back to being a set-piece bet rather than a defender.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: Wissa scored at Spurs and is being described as reborn under Jaissle, and the Sunday gossip has Napoli asking about a loan. The seat was the whole case and it is no longer clear.
verdicts.trigger: A league start ahead of Wissa. Short of that this is the wrong Newcastle forward at the same £6.0m.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by three of the five, at a club that has spent £300m and sits bottom after losing at home to Newcastle. Still no clean sheet.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Tonali
verdicts.why: The trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle. He was substituted, was rated the worst of the Spurs midfield, and the away end sang about the score at him.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. A £5.5m midfielder being managed back to fitness at a bottom club is not an asset.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for — and Mukiele’s fitness is what would put him back.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created at £6.0m, in a side being publicly written off as relegation candidates.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Igor Jesus
verdicts.why: He started at Anfield ahead of the club-record signing and forced a fine save from Alisson before half-time. That is one of the two starts his trigger asked for.
verdicts.trigger: One more start with Delap fit and £6.0m is a buy. Left out at Villa Park and it is over.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: Seventeen points at £4.6m, and Brighton go to Stamford Bridge without Mitoma, Minteh and Tzimas and with two more flagged — the attacking returns were the case and the attack is the injured part.
verdicts.trigger: A second attacking return with that forward line unavailable, and this is a buy rather than an argument.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick — but the next one is at Chelsea.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

verdicts.name: Foden
verdicts.why: £7.0m and 4.1% owned in the City attack, and he released Haaland for the fourth at Palace after a week in which his manager kept picking him.
verdicts.trigger: A start missed once Doku is back on 5 September. At 4% ownership the risk is minutes, not returns.

verdicts.name: O'Reilly
verdicts.why: £6.5m and 20% owned, and Maresca pushed him high in a 4-1-4-1 instead of leaving him at left-back. A defender used as a midfielder is priced for clean sheets he is not there to keep.
verdicts.trigger: Two games back in the defensive line, or a goal from the advanced role. Either one settles which player is being bought.

verdicts.name: Muñoz
verdicts.why: Settled. Forest have agreed a minimum £22m and he has permission for a medical, reuniting him with Glasner. Palace expect Khalaili to take the shirt.
verdicts.trigger: Settled by the transfer. Nothing left here.

verdicts.name: Delap
verdicts.why: The trigger was one start ahead of Igor Jesus. He did not get it at Anfield, four days after the £45m was paid.
verdicts.trigger: Named at Villa Park. A club-record striker who does not start his second game is a substitute at any price.

verdicts.name: Isak
verdicts.why: Six touches and no shots in the first half at Anfield, then the equaliser with his ninth. Hart said Liverpool have not worked out how to play with him and the trust is not there.
verdicts.trigger: Two games with double figures for touches. At £9.0m the problem is service, not finishing, and service takes weeks.

verdicts.name: Gibbs-White
verdicts.why: The best player at Anfield on Saturday and the penalty scorer, on fifteen points at £7.9m with 8% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Forest's new front line settling and the penalties moving with it. Nothing else here is in doubt.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Scored at Spurs and has been described as reborn under Jaissle. Seventeen points at £6.0m, 3% owned, in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: The £52m Gonzalez or Fernandez-Pardo taking his flank. A cheap winger at a club still buying wingers is a minutes bet.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Scored at Spurs at £6.0m and 4.5% ownership, in the striker slot two of these pages have spent a fortnight giving to Woltemade.
verdicts.trigger: A second league start ahead of Woltemade, and this is the Newcastle forward to own.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: Twenty points from a £4.0m defender at a side that has won both games and conceded nothing. The 75% flag that made the brain decline him has cleared.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the back four, or a Hull goal conceded pattern once the fixtures harden. Villa at home in GW3 is the honest test.

verdicts.name: Mendy
verdicts.why: Sixteen points at £4.0m in the same clean-sheet defence, and he had a shot from thirty yards at Coventry. The flag has cleared here too.
verdicts.trigger: Hull have made thirteen signings this window. One rotation and a £4.0m defender is a bench place.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: Twenty points at £4.5m from two clean sheets, with saves that kept Coventry out on Saturday. The cheapest goalkeeper bracket has produced the best goalkeeper so far.
verdicts.trigger: Villa at home, then Chelsea away. Two clean sheets in those and this is the goalkeeper of the first quarter.

verdicts.name: Scott
verdicts.why: Fourteen points at £6.0m and 1.6% ownership, and Bournemouth's manager was asked about the interest in him rather than about the draw.
verdicts.trigger: A move before Tuesday, or two more weeks of returns. Buying into an open window is how the last three of these went wrong.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: A £5.4m City defender with no points and 0.7% ownership, behind O'Reilly and Gvardiol in a back line that is rearranged weekly.
verdicts.trigger: A start. Until then this is a bench place doing no work for the one gaffer who owns him.

signals.text: Alonso dropped him after his part in both Fulham goals and Chelsea signed Emiliano Martinez for £7.5m. "Sánchez needs to leave. He will be frozen out if he stays and looks unlikely to feature when Chelsea host Brighton on Sunday."
signals.action: settled. The Chelsea goalkeeper slot belongs to a 33-year-old World Cup winner on a two-year deal

signals.text: City made formal contact with Liverpool on Saturday evening, and City is his preferred destination if he leaves before Tuesday. Liverpool would prefer to sign another forward first.
signals.action: a goal and an assist in two games at £7.0m, and three days to find out whether he is still a Liverpool player on Friday

signals.text: Six touches, one accurate pass and no shots in the first half against Forest, then the equaliser with his ninth touch. Hart: "At Liverpool that trust just isn't there at the moment — he isn't that central point, which is leading to him looking lost and isolated."
signals.action: £9.0m for a striker whose team has not worked out how to feed him. Wait for the service, not the finishing

signals.text: "A poor display from the Liverpool left-back and was sloppy in possession. Replaced by Kostas Tsimikas in the 71st minute."
signals.action: one point from two full games and now a substitution. Xabi is the one holding him

signals.text: Substituted in the 2-0 home defeat by his old club, with the Newcastle end taunting him about the score. Rated the poorest of the Spurs midfield after a £100m move.
signals.action: his trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle. It fired the wrong way, so the £5.5m case is closed

signals.text: Headed a late equaliser at Bournemouth to rescue a point, four days after the brain wrote that a goal or a clean sheet there was the whole test.
signals.action: trigger met. Eighteen points at £6.0m and nobody in the five owns him

signals.text: Scored in the 2-0 win at Spurs. "A number of the players Jaissle inherited, such as goalscorers Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa, also look reborn."
signals.action: seventeen points at £6.0m and 3% ownership, in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker

signals.text: Wissa scored at Spurs, and Sunday's gossip column reports Napoli interest in taking Woltemade on loan before Tuesday.
signals.action: the seat was the whole case for him at £6.0m. Wissa is the same price and has just scored

signals.text: Scored the penalty that put Forest ahead for the second time at Anfield and was the best player on the pitch by the ratings.
signals.action: fifteen points at £7.9m and 8% owned, and nobody in the room has a Forest midfielder

signals.text: Started at Anfield ahead of the £45m club-record signing and forced a superb save from Alisson on the brink of half-time.
signals.action: one of the two starts his trigger asked for. Delap did not get his

signals.text: Forest have agreed a deal worth a minimum of £22m and he has permission for a medical. Palace expect Khalaili to take his place.
signals.action: settled. A £5.5m Palace defender who is having a medical elsewhere is not a GW3 buy

signals.text: "Confidence and desire — why Bournemouth's Scott is in demand." Fourteen points at £6.0m and 1.6% ownership, three days from the deadline.
signals.action: the returns are real and the club is not settled. D9 says wait until Wednesday

signals.text: Two wins from two and two clean sheets, Millar's 82nd-minute winner at Coventry, and thirteen arrivals this window including a £20m forward from Union Berlin and Ali-Cho, who debuted late on.
signals.action: the £4.0m Hull defenders now have two clean sheets behind them rather than one haul. Thirteen signings means checking the team sheet before Friday

signals.text: Two draws from two under Iraola and four goals conceded, with Mac Allister restored to the midfield, Victor Munoz given a first start on the left and the back line cut open for Forest's opener.
signals.action: Liverpool defenders are not clean-sheet buys yet. Ipswich away in GW3 is the softest test they will get to prove otherwise

signals.text: £300m spent and bottom of the table after losing 2-0 at home to Newcastle. De Zerbi said Spurs "didn't deserve" the loss and that he is not angry.
signals.action: three of the five own the Spurs goalkeeper and one owns two of them. No clean sheet yet and no reason to expect one in GW3

signals.text: First league win under Jaissle, with Elanga and Wissa scoring and the £52m Nico González impressing on debut as what one reporter called a quarterback. Fernandez-Pardo of Lille is still being chased.
signals.action: buy the Newcastle wide players rather than the striker slot. Wissa and Woltemade are the same price and only one of them has scored

signals.text: Martinez signed for £7.5m on a two-year deal and Sánchez dropped, with Chelsea expecting to move him on before Tuesday. Penders stays as the long-term choice with a mentor above him.
signals.action: a settled goalkeeper is worth something to Chelsea defenders. Arsenal away in GW3 is not where you find out

signals.text: Muñoz has permission for a Forest medical after a £22m agreement, Lacroix has gone to Chelsea, Mateta is out and Sarr is unavailable. Two games, no points.
signals.action: no Palace defender is a GW3 buy, and Fulham away does not change that

signals.text: Forest have bid £40m for Armstrong, who started at Bournemouth while the away end chanted that there would be a riot if he was sold. Moyes: "Supporters aren't always wrong." Still no right-back and no striker.
signals.action: the Everton midfield is the buyable part of this club and its two best names are both being bid for. Nothing here is safe until Tuesday night

signals.text: Igor Jesus started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, McAtee came in for the departed Anderson and Schlager for the injured I.Sangaré, and Muñoz is arriving from Palace.
signals.action: leave the Forest front line until an eleven repeats itself. The midfield is the part that is already picking itself

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend’s best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room’s bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.
An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. Buy after the window shuts, not into it.

A cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything — which is why a 35-year-old’s header, a flagged striker’s replacement and a vice-captain’s absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes. Two calls were resolved this week without a ball being kicked: the Chelsea goalkeeper, because Chelsea signed one, and the Liverpool winger, because Liverpool bought over him. A trigger that only a scoreline can fire will sit open through the weeks that actually decide the player.

A room that agrees has no insurance. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week — the three who did in GW1 all moved off him — and he scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has quietly agreed on, not only what it argues about.

Grade a rule by what it cost, not by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no is not a rule, it is a mood.

roast.text: Mr CR7 left twelve points on his bench, nine of them Gvardiol, playing at the Etihad. Somewhere in that team sheet is a man who looked at a City defender at home and decided it was too risky.

plan.outlook: Half of Gameweek 2 has been played and the room is still waiting on the half that matters. Four of the five need B.Fernandes at home to Ipswich, The Special One needs João Pedro against Brighton, and Le Professeur needs Cash to survive Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday. What has already happened has mostly happened to players nobody owns. Newcastle won at Spurs through two £6.0m forwards, Tarkowski scored the goal his trigger asked for, and Hull won again without conceding while their two £4.0m defenders sat unowned in every squad. Le Professeur leads by a point from Mr CR7, and Sir Fergie has spent a Bench Boost to close within seven. The real work is Tuesday to Friday. The window shuts on Tuesday night, the GW3 deadline is the Friday after, and for the first time this season the team sheets can be known before the money is spent. Cherki, Ajayi and Tarkowski are the three names to have an answer ready for.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). Two Bench Boosts have gone in the room's first two weeks, both before a double gameweek exists. This week's covered a second goalkeeper, two £4.0m Coventry defenders and a Brighton midfielder, which is four squad players rather than a bench. A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded, but that was neither. The first real chip conversation is GW6–8: window shut a fortnight, three settled line-ups, and a fixture run you can read.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.
